newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Acting Russian defence minister lifelong rocketman.
newsitem.headline: Acting Russian defence minister lifelong rocketman.

text.p: New acting defence minister Igor Sergeyev is a 30-year veteran of Russia's nuclear missile force but he could be a stopgap until President Boris Yeltsin finds a minister to complete much-needed military reform.
Sergeyev, 59, has headed the Strategic Rocket Forces since 1992, responsible the 756 ICBM missiles with 3,535 nuclear warheads which making up Russia's strategic arsenal.
He took acting command of the defence ministry after Russian President Boris Yeltsin dismissed Igor Rodionov on Thursday.
"He is very intelligent, a very, very nice guy. He's the first chief of the rocket force who has risen through the silos," said Pavel Felgengauer, defence expert for the daily newspaper Sevodnya.
"He has good contacts with the West...He is most likely a stopgap," Felgengauer added, noting that Sergeyev could find little support from tank troops or from the navy or air force.

Sergeyev, a bespectacled, silver-haired man who looks older than his 59 years, has said he views Russia's nuclear forces as the backbone of its defence, and describes it as one that is especially economical in a time of spending cutbacks.

"The Strategic Missile Troops can evolve into a real nucleus of Russian military might, which will ensure strategic stability in the world, deterence and the maintenance of Russia's status as a great power," he said recently.
Sergeyev has also spoken out in favor of a START-3 nuclear arms reduction agreement with the United States as an extension of the START-2 accord cutting the Russian and American nuclear arsenals.

He has also argued for a political accord with NATO to prevent the stationing of nuclear forces on the territory of new eastern European members the Western alliance is expected to invite into NATO in July.

Sergeyev was born in 1938 into a mining family and then attended a naval academy on the Black Sea. He started serving with the missile forces at the height of the Cold War in 1961 and gradually moved up the command ladder.
Married with a son, Sergeyev is said to be a fan of sport and classical literature in his spare time.
